title: Spatial Relation and Abstract Reasoning
html:
The last block of the Mental Agility Test — 5 of the 20 questions — is the only one asked in pictures. MEC calls it spatial relation / abstract reasoning, and its two official sample questions show the range: which 3D shape can be made from this 2D net? and which shape completes this sequence? Around them sit the other standard picture types: dice, mirror and water images, folded and punched paper, hidden (embedded) figures and counting figures. These questions reward a fixed routine more than talent: for nets, find the opposite faces first; for images, decide what is swapped; for paper, unfold one fold at a time; for series, follow one element at a time. In the practice sets the figure comes first; read it fully before the question.

What the paper asks from this chapter
  • Nets: in a straight line of three squares the first and third are opposite; at the two ends of a Z the end squares are opposite. Opposite faces are never seen together.
  • Which cube? Around any face, the neighbours keep the clockwise order they have in the net.
  • Dice: a face seen together with X is not opposite X; on a standard die opposite faces add to 7.
  • Painted cube cut into n^3 small cubes: 8 with three faces painted, 12(n-2) with two, 6(n-2)^2 with one, (n-2)^3 with none.
  • Mirror image: left and right swap (the order of letters reverses); water image: top and bottom swap (the order stays).
  • Paper folding: every hole is reflected in every fold line; k folds in half give 2^k holes from one punch.
  • Counting: count systematically — by corners or by sizes — or use the formula for the standard figure.
  • Series and matrices: track each element (position, rotation, number, shading) separately; each must follow its own rule.

4.1 Nets, cubes and dice

Faces, edges and corners

A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners (vertices). Each face shares an edge with 4 faces and is opposite exactly one. Three faces meet at every corner, so a picture of a cube shows three faces that are pairwise adjacent — two opposite faces can never be seen together.

Nets

A net is a flat pattern of six squares that folds into a cube. There are exactly 11 of them. Learn to see the opposite pairs at once:

  1. Line of three. In a straight row (or column) of three squares, the first and the third are opposite.
  2. Z rule. When four squares form a Z or S (two squares, a step, two squares), the two end squares are opposite.
  3. Squares that share an edge in the net are always adjacent on the cube.

A pattern is not a net if it has four squares in a 2 × 2 block, five or more in a straight line, or if the rules above give some face two different opposites.

Which cube can be made from the net?

Check the options in this order:

  1. Opposite faces. Find the three opposite pairs from the net. Any option that shows two opposite faces together is wrong — this alone settles most questions.
  2. Order round a face. Look at the top face of the option and find it in the net. Looking at the top face from outside, its four neighbours keep the order they have round it in the net. In a drawing that shows the top, the left-front and the right-front faces, the right face comes just before the left face when you go clockwise round the top face.

A neighbour that is not joined to the top square in the net can still be placed: fold the joined neighbours down first and see where the next square lands.

Opposite faces from a net

Problem. In a cross-shaped net the middle row is P, Q, R, S, with T above Q and U below Q. Which face is opposite Q, and which is opposite T?

Solution. The middle row is a line of four: P–R are opposite (first and third of P, Q, R) and Q–S are opposite (first and third of Q, R, S). The column T, Q, U is a line of three, so T is opposite U. Opposite Q is S.

Dice

A die is a cube with the numbers 1 to 6 on its faces. On a standard die opposite faces add up to 7: 1–6, 2–5, 3–4. When a question shows several positions of one die, do not assume it is standard — work from the pictures:

  1. Every number seen together with X in any picture is adjacent to X.
  2. X has four neighbours; the one number never seen with X is opposite it.
  3. If that leaves two candidates, look for a picture that links them to faces already placed.
Two positions of a die

Problem. One position of a die shows 1 on top with 2 and 3 on the sides; another shows 1 on top with 4 and 6 on the sides. Which number is opposite 1?

Solution. 1 is seen with 2, 3, 4 and 6 — its four neighbours. The only number left is 5, which is opposite 1. (This die is not standard.)

The painted cube

A cube painted on all its faces is cut into n \times n \times n equal small cubes. Where a small cube sits decides how many painted faces it has:

Position Painted faces Number of small cubes n = 3 n = 4 n = 5
Corner 3 8 8 8 8
Edge (not corner) 2 12(n - 2) 12 24 36
Face (not edge) 1 6(n - 2)^2 6 24 54
Inside 0 (n - 2)^3 1 8 27
Total n^3 27 64 125
A cuboid

Problem. A painted cuboid 4 cm × 3 cm × 2 cm is cut into 1 cm cubes. How many cubes have exactly two painted faces?

Solution. Two-face cubes lie on the edges, not at the corners. A cuboid has 4 edges of each length: 4 × (4 − 2) + 4 × (3 − 2) + 4 × (2 − 2) = 8 + 4 + 0 = 12. (Check: 8 corner cubes + 12 + 4 one-face cubes = 24 cubes in all.)

Do not count the corners twice

A corner cube touches three faces and three edges. In the "two faces painted" count it must be left out: an edge of 4 small cubes has only 4 − 2 = 2 two-face cubes.

4.2 Mirror and water images

A mirror image is the reflection in a mirror held upright beside the object: left and right are interchanged, top and bottom are not. A word's letters come in the reverse order, and each letter is itself flipped. A water image is the reflection in a horizontal surface below the object: top and bottom are interchanged, left and right are not — the letters keep their order but each is upside down.

Capital letters that look the same Letters
in a mirror (vertical line of symmetry) A, H, I, M, O, T, U, V, W, X, Y
in water (horizontal line of symmetry) B, C, D, E, H, I, K, O, X
in both H, I, O, X

A word looks the same in a mirror only if every letter is in the first row and the word reads the same backwards: MOM, WOW, TOOT (TOY is not — it becomes YOT). A word looks the same in water if every letter is in the second row, because the order does not change: BOX, HIDE, DECIDE.

Clocks. For a clock seen in a mirror beside it, real time = 11:60 − time seen (Unit 3). A mirror followed by a water image is the same as turning the figure through 180°.

Picking the mirror image

Problem. How do you choose the mirror image of a word from four options?

Solution. Check two things. (1) Order: the last letter of the word must come first. (2) Shape: an asymmetric letter (such as N, P, G, L) must be flipped. The two classic wrong options each fail one test: the word written backwards with normal letters, and the word in the right order with each letter flipped. A third wrong option is usually the water image (letters upside down).

4.3 Paper folding and cutting

A sheet is folded one or more times, and a hole (or a cut) is made through all the layers. When it is unfolded:

  1. Count. Each fold in half doubles the layers: one punch through k folds in half gives 2^k holes.
  2. Place. Unfold in reverse order. Each time, every hole is reflected in the fold line being opened — the same distance on the other side of the line.
  3. Shape. A cut on a fold line opens into a symmetric shape: a half-circle cut on the fold opens into a full circle.

Unfold one fold at a time

Problem. A square sheet is folded left onto right and then top onto bottom, and one hole is punched near the outer corner of the folded square (the corner that was the bottom-right corner of the sheet). Where are the holes on the opened sheet?

Solution. Open the second fold first: the hole is reflected in the horizontal fold line, giving two holes one above the other. Open the first fold: both are reflected in the vertical fold line. Four holes, one near each corner of the sheet (figure above). Had the hole been punched near the inner corner of the folded square, the four holes would sit round the centre of the sheet instead.

A hole is reflected, not copied

A hole near the right edge of the folded paper reappears near the left edge after opening a vertical fold — not in the same place on the other half. And a diagonal fold reflects in that diagonal: a hole near the bottom edge reappears near the left edge.

4.4 Embedded figures and counting figures

Embedded (hidden) figures

The given figure X is hidden in one of the options, with the same size, the same shape and the same way up — not rotated, not reflected. Find the most unusual part of X (an odd angle, a short tail, a small closed shape), look for it in each option, and then check every line of X against the option. Options that contain X turned over, rotated, stretched or with one line moved are the standard distractors.

Counting figures

Count with a system, never by eye:

  • Label the points and list the figures by their corners.
  • Count by size: smallest pieces first, then figures made of two pieces, three, …
  • Use a formula for a standard figure.
Figure Count
Triangle with n lines from the top corner to the base (n + 1)(n + 2)/2 triangles
The same with h lines across, parallel to the base (base included) h × (n + 1)(n + 2)/2
Square with both diagonals 8 triangles
Square with both diagonals and both mid-lines 16 triangles
n × n grid of squares 1^2 + 2^2 + \dots + n^2 squares (3 × 3: 14; 4 × 4: 30)
m × n grid \frac{m(m+1)}{2} \times \frac{n(n+1)}{2} rectangles (2 × 2: 9; 3 × 3: 36)

Counting triangles

Problem. How many triangles are there in the figure above?

Solution. Every triangle has A as one corner and two of the base points B, P, Q, R, C as the others. Choosing 2 points out of 5 gives 5 × 4/2 = 10 triangles. (By sizes: 4 single pieces, 3 made of two, 2 of three, 1 of four: 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10.)

4.5 Figure series, analogies and matrices

Series

A figure series changes by a fixed rule from one step to the next. The elements that change are few:

Element Typical rule
Position moves one corner (or 45°, 90°) clockwise or anticlockwise each step
Rotation turns through 45°, 90° or 180° each step
Number one more (or one fewer) dot, line or side each step
Shading alternates, or moves round the parts of the figure
Size grows or shrinks each step

Method. Follow one element across all the steps and write its rule; then the next element. For each rule, cross out the options that break it. Usually one element removes two options and a second element removes the third.

Two elements at once

Problem. In the series above (steps 1 to 4), what does step 5 look like?

Solution. The dot visits the corners top-left → top-right → bottom-right → bottom-left: clockwise, one corner per step, so step 5 is top-left again. The arrow points up → left → down → right: 90° anticlockwise each step, so step 5 points up. Step 5: dot at top-left, arrow up (shaded).

Analogies

Figure 1 : figure 2 :: figure 3 : ? — find what was done to figure 1 to give figure 2 (rotated 90° clockwise, reflected, shading reversed, a line added, the inner and outer shapes swapped) and do exactly that to figure 3. With rotations, check the direction: a rotation by 90° clockwise and a reflection can look alike for a shape with symmetry, so test a shape with no symmetry.

Matrices

In a 3 × 3 matrix each row (and often each column) follows the same rule. Common rules:

  • each row contains one of each of three shapes (a Latin square);
  • a count increases along the row (1, 2, 3 dots);
  • the third figure is the first two laid on top of each other, or keeps only the lines that are not common to both.

Find the rule in the two complete rows, check it on the columns, then apply it to the row with the gap.

Eliminate, then confirm

In figure questions, the fastest route is elimination: test one feature at a time and cross out options. Once one option is left, confirm it against all the rules — the setters build a distractor that is right in every feature but one.

Formula and fact sheet

Topic Fact
Cube 6 faces, 12 edges, 8 corners; each face has 4 neighbours and 1 opposite
Nets 11 nets; line of three → ends opposite; Z shape → ends opposite
Not a net a 2 × 2 block, 5 in a row, or a face with two opposites
Which cube opposite faces never together; neighbours keep their clockwise order round a face
Standard die opposite faces add to 7: 1–6, 2–5, 3–4
Die from views a face seen with X is adjacent; the one never seen with X is opposite
Painted cube (n^3 pieces) 3 faces: 8; 2 faces: 12(n-2); 1 face: 6(n-2)^2; none: (n-2)^3
Painted cuboid two-face cubes: 4 × [(a − 2) + (b − 2) + (c − 2)]
Mirror image left–right swap; letter order reverses; A H I M O T U V W X Y unchanged
Water image top–bottom swap; order unchanged; B C D E H I K O X unchanged
Mirror + water = rotation through 180°
Mirror clock real time = 11:60 − time seen
Paper folding k folds in half → 2^k holes; unfold in reverse, reflect in each fold line
Triangles n lines from the apex: (n+1)(n+2)/2; × h with h cross lines
Squares in n × n grid 1^2 + 2^2 + \dots + n^2
Rectangles in m × n grid \frac{m(m+1)}{2} \times \frac{n(n+1)}{2}
Series track position, rotation, number, shading, size — one at a time

Chapter summary

  • Spatial relation / abstract reasoning carries 5 of the 20 MAT questions; the MEC samples are a net → cube question and a figure-sequence question.
  • Nets: find the opposite pairs (line of three, Z rule); options showing two opposite faces together are wrong; the remaining ones are decided by the clockwise order of the neighbours round a face.
  • Dice: faces seen together are adjacent; the face never seen with X is opposite X; a standard die has opposite faces adding to 7.
  • Painted cubes: 8, 12(n-2), 6(n-2)^2, (n-2)^3 for three, two, one and no painted faces.
  • Mirror image swaps left and right (reversed order, flipped letters); water image swaps top and bottom (same order).
  • Folded paper: 2^k holes from k folds; unfold in reverse, reflecting every hole in each fold line.
  • Count figures systematically, by corners or by sizes, or with the standard formulas.
  • Series, analogies and matrices: follow one element at a time and eliminate options.

Practice questions

  2. A cube of side 4 cm is cut into cubes of side 1 cm. How many small cubes are obtained?a16b64c32d48
  3. A cube painted on all its faces is cut into 27 equal small cubes. How many small cubes have three painted faces?a8b4c12d6
Answers and explanations — Set A

1. (a) — 3 + 4 = 7.

2. (c) — A face has four edges and shares each with one neighbour; only the opposite face is not a neighbour.

3. (b) — A, C, F are a column of three: the first and third, A and F, are opposite.

4. (a) — B, C, D are a row of three, so B and D are opposite (and C is opposite E).

5. (d) — There are exactly 11 nets of a cube.

6. (c) — 4 edges round the top, 4 round the bottom and 4 upright: 12.

7. (b) — n = 3: 12(n − 2) = 12. One middle cube on each of the 12 edges.

8. (a) — (n − 2)³ = 1: only the centre cube is hidden from every face.

9. (c) — 2 is seen with 1 and 4 in (i) and with 5 and 3 in (ii): its four neighbours are 1, 3, 4, 5. The number never seen with 2 is 6, so 6 is opposite 2.

10. (b) — n = 4: 6(n − 2)² = 6 × 4 = 24 (the 2 × 2 centre of each face).

11. (d) — Faces at a corner are pairwise adjacent, so no two may add to 7. Each other option contains an opposite pair (1–6, 2–5, 3–4).

12. (b) — In a mirror the letter order reverses and each letter is flipped. MOM reads the same backwards and M and O are symmetric left to right. D, N and P are not.

13. (c) — The water image keeps the order but turns each letter upside down; B, O and X are symmetric top to bottom. M, A, T, Y and W are not.

14. (d) — A, H and T have a vertical line of symmetry; N does not (its mirror image is И).

15. (a) — The mirror image reverses the order (C first) and flips every letter. (b) only reverses the order, (c) only flips the letters, (d) is the water image.

16. (b) — A horizontal mirror below the figure interchanges top and bottom only.

17. (b) — The arrow turns 45° clockwise each step: up, up-right, right, down-right, so next is down.

18. (c) — Two folds in half give 2² = 4 layers, so one punch makes 4 holes.

19. (d) — 9 small squares + 4 squares of side 2 + 1 of side 3 = 14.

20. (a) — The hole is reflected in the fold line: the same height, the same distance on the left of the fold. Option (b) reflects it in a horizontal line instead; (c) forgets the second layer.

21. (d) — (2 × 3/2) × (2 × 3/2) = 3 × 3 = 9: 4 small squares, 2 + 2 two-square rectangles and the whole square.

22. (c) — 4 small triangles and 4 made of two small ones (each half of the square): 8.

23. (c) — Two lines from the top corner divide the base into 3 parts: the triangles are chosen by 2 of the 4 base points, (2 + 1)(2 + 2)/2 = 6.

24. (b) — 4 × 4 × 4 = 64.

25. (a) — The three-face cubes are the 8 corners, for any n ≥ 2.

Set B — Understanding (15 questions)

  1. In the figure above, which cube can be made from the net?acube abcube bccube cdcube d

  1. In the figure above, which number is opposite 4?a1b5c6d2

  1. In the figure above, which arrangement can NOT be folded into a cube?ashape abshape bcshape cdshape d
  2. A cube painted on all its faces is cut into 64 equal small cubes. How many small cubes have no painted face?a16b4c24d8
  3. A cube painted on all its faces is cut into 125 equal small cubes. How many small cubes have exactly two painted faces?a24b36c48d54
  4. A cube painted on all its faces is cut into 64 equal small cubes. How many small cubes have at least one painted face?a56b48c60d8

  1. In the figure above, which option is the water image of the word?aimage abimage bcimage cdimage d

  1. In the figure above, which option shows the sheet when it is unfolded?asheet absheet bcsheet cdsheet d

  1. In the figure above, which option comes next in the series?afigure abfigure bcfigure cdfigure d

  1. In the figure above, which option completes the analogy?afigure abfigure bcfigure cdfigure d

  1. How many triangles are there in the figure above?a9b10c12d6
  2. How many squares of all sizes are there in a 4 × 4 grid of squares?a30b16c25d20
  3. How many rectangles of all sizes (squares included) are there in a 3 × 3 grid of squares?a14b36c9d30
  4. On a standard die, 2 and 3 are on two neighbouring faces. Which number can be on a face that touches both of them?a4b5c6d3
  5. In a mirror held beside a wall clock, the clock appears to show 2:30. What is the actual time?a9:30b10:30c9:00d8:30
Answers and explanations — Set B

1. (c) — Opposite pairs from the net: ring–bullseye (row of three), dot–grey (ends of the Z dot, black, ring, grey) and black–blank (ends of the Z black, ring, grey, blank). (a) shows dot with grey, (b) ring with bullseye and (d) black with blank — each shows an opposite pair. In (c), with black on top, the ring folds down in front and the grey square, joined to the ring's right edge, comes round to the right.

2. (b) — 4 is seen with 3 and 2 in (i), with 1 and 3 in (ii) and with 6 and 2 in (iii): its neighbours are 1, 2, 3, 6. The number never seen with 4 is 5.

3. (a) — In shape (a) the top row is a line of three, so its first and third squares are opposite; the third square, the next two and the last one form a Z, so the same third square is also opposite the last square. A face cannot have two opposites, so (a) cannot fold. (b), (c) and (d) are among the 11 nets.

4. (d) — n = 4: (n − 2)³ = 2³ = 8 hidden cubes.

5. (b) — n = 5: 12(n − 2) = 12 × 3 = 36.

6. (a) — All 64 minus the 8 unpainted inner cubes: 56.

7. (d) — A water image keeps the letters in the same order and turns each upside down. (a) is the mirror image, (c) the figure turned through 180°, and (b) also reverses the order.

8. (b) — The packet is the bottom-right quarter, and the hole is near its bottom edge, midway across. Opening the second fold reflects it in the vertical centre line (a second hole near the bottom edge); opening the first reflects both in the horizontal centre line (two holes near the top edge). (c) puts the holes near the side edges instead; (a) and (d) leave out holes.

9. (d) — The dots increase by one (1, 2, 3, 4 → 5) and the shaded corner moves clockwise (top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left → top-left). Only (d) has five dots and the top-left corner.

10. (c) — The flag is turned through 90° clockwise. Turning the F through 90° clockwise puts its upright stroke along the top, with both bars hanging down. (a) is turned anticlockwise and (b) is a mirror image.

11. (c) — Two lines from the top corner make (2 + 1)(2 + 2)/2 = 6 triangles on the base; the cross line makes another 6 above it: 2 × 6 = 12.

12. (a) — 16 + 9 + 4 + 1 = 30.

13. (b) — (3 × 4/2) × (3 × 4/2) = 6 × 6 = 36. 14 counts only the squares.

14. (c) — The faces touching both 2 and 3 are those opposite neither: not 5 (opposite 2) and not 4 (opposite 3). So 1 or 6; of the options only 6.

15. (a) — 11:60 − 2:30 = 9:30.

Set C — Application (10 questions)

  1. In the figure above, which cube can be made from the net?acube abcube bccube cdcube d

  1. In the figure above, which option shows the sheet when it is unfolded?asheet absheet bcsheet cdsheet d

  1. In the figure above, which option replaces the question mark?afigure abfigure bcfigure cdfigure d

  1. In the figure above, in which option is figure X embedded?afigure abfigure bcfigure cdfigure d

  1. How many triangles are there in the figure above?a16b12c24d20
  2. A 4 × 4 × 4 cube is painted on two opposite faces only and then cut into 64 unit cubes. How many unit cubes have no paint at all?a16b32c48d8
  3. A cuboid 5 cm × 4 cm × 3 cm is painted on all its faces and cut into 1 cm cubes. How many cubes have exactly two painted faces?a22b12c24d36
  4. A cube painted on all its faces is cut into equal small cubes, and exactly 8 of the small cubes have no paint. How many small cubes have exactly one painted face?a24b8c48d36
  5. A word is reflected in an upright mirror, and that image is then reflected in a horizontal mirror below it. Compared with the original word, the final image isaturned through 90° clockwisebturned through 180°cturned through 90° anticlockwisedunchanged
  6. A cube painted blue on all its faces is cut into 8 equal small cubes. How many faces of the small cubes, in all, are unpainted?a8b16c24d48
Answers and explanations — Set C

1. (d) — Opposite pairs (Z rule): ring–black, dot–grey, bullseye–blank; no option shows a pair, so fold. Put the bullseye on top: the dot folds to the back and black to the right; grey, joined to the lower edge of black, comes round to the front; the ring goes to the left. So with the bullseye on top, grey is in front and black on the right: (d). (a) swaps them (a mirror image). In (c), with the bullseye on top and the dot in front, the right face would be the ring, not black. In (b), with the dot on top and the bullseye in front, the right face would be black, not the ring.

2. (c) — The hole is near the bottom edge, a little right of its middle. Opening the second fold reflects it in the line from the bottom-left corner to the centre: a second hole near the left edge, a little above its middle. Opening the diagonal fold reflects both in the other diagonal: holes near the right edge (a little below its middle) and near the top edge (a little left of its middle) — a "pinwheel" of four holes, symmetric about both diagonals. (d) is symmetric about one diagonal only, (b) about the mid-lines instead of the diagonals, and (a) has only two holes although the punch went through four layers.

3. (a) — Each row contains one circle, one square and one triangle, so the gap is a square; the dots go 1, 2, 3 along every row, so it has 3 dots.

4. (b) — (b) has the triangle the same way up, the same size, with the short line hanging from the middle of its base. (a) is upside down, in (c) the short line is not at the middle, and in (d) the triangle is taller.

5. (d) — The square with its two diagonals already holds 8 triangles (4 quarters and 4 halves). The inner lines cut off a triangle at each corner, and the diagonal splits it into two small ones: 3 triangles per corner, 12 in all. The four pieces inside the inner square are squares, not triangles. Total 8 + 12 = 20.

6. (b) — The two painted faces each hold 16 cubes, so 32 cubes have paint and 64 − 32 = 32 have none.

7. (c) — Two-face cubes lie on the 12 edges, corners left out: 4 × (5 − 2) + 4 × (4 − 2) + 4 × (3 − 2) = 12 + 8 + 4 = 24. (22 is the number with one painted face.)

8. (a) — (n − 2)³ = 8 gives n = 4. One-face cubes: 6(n − 2)² = 6 × 4 = 24.

9. (b) — The mirror swaps left and right, the water image swaps top and bottom; doing both is a half-turn (180°).

10. (c) — Each of the 8 small cubes is a corner cube with 3 painted and 3 unpainted faces: 8 × 3 = 24.
